deities: Banke Bihari (Krishna in the Tribhanga, three-fold-bent posture, embodying Radha-Krishna)

history.dynasty: 19th century (followers of Swami Haridas; cared for by the Goswami descendants)
history.summary: The soul of Vrindavan and one of India's most visited Krishna temples. The deity manifested to the 16th-century saint-musician Swami Haridas (guru of Tansen) in the sacred grove of Nidhivan, drawn out by his devotional song; the black idol in the Tribhanga posture ('banke' = bent in three places) is treated as combining Radha and Krishna, and its lotus feet are kept permanently veiled. The present Rajasthani-style temple with carved arched ceilings was built in 1864 to house the idol after its move from Nidhivan, and is cared for by the Goswami descendants of Swami Haridas. Unique customs: jhanki darshan - a curtain is drawn before the idol every 1-2 minutes so Bihari Ji (worshipped as a child, not awakened) will not follow a devotee home; no bells, no conch, no Mangala Aarti; soft music only. The Phool Bangla Seva dresses the sanctum in elaborate flower structures.

name: Banke Bihari Temple
town_description: Vrindavan, on the Yamuna in Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh, is the sacred playground (leelasthali) of Krishna's youth and the heart of Braj bhumi. It hosts some of Hinduism's most beloved shrines - Banke Bihari, Radha Raman, Rangji, ISKCON's Krishna Balaram Mandir and Prem Mandir - and draws millions of pilgrims, especially for Holi and Janmashtami.

travel.railway: Mathura Junction, ~12 km; Vrindavan has its own small railhead (verify)
travel.road: Shri Banke Bihari Marg, Goda Vihar, Vrindavan 281121; ~12 km from Mathura city, ~70 km from Agra; photography and phones prohibited inside; dress code enforced (shoulders and knees covered)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami, Holi, Radhashtami and Sharad Purnima for grand celebrations (extremely crowded); weekday mornings for calmer darshan
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer (Apr-Oct): 7:45 AM-12:00 noon and 5:30-9:30 PM; Winter (Nov-Mar): 8:45 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-8:30 PM; closed between sessions and during Rajbhog/Shayan aartis (per mathuravrindavan.info and darshantiming.com)
